# Chromium T-Rex Runner

The embedded T-Rex Runner uses the official Chromium implementation, art, and
sounds from Chromium Stable 151.0.7922.77 at commit
`ff37cfca210138f2a40b843b4a8195ab7e4fc7ff`. The audited Chromium `main`
snapshot at `700a8854c734478efbf6e205936983b64f9f53df` was byte-identical for the
vendored game source and selected assets.

- Project: <https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/>
- Game source: <https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/ff37cfca210138f2a40b843b4a8195ab7e4fc7ff/components/neterror/resources/dino_game/>
- Net error resources: <https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/ff37cfca210138f2a40b843b4a8195ab7e4fc7ff/components/neterror/resources/>
- License: [`front-end/public/licenses/chromium-bsd-license.txt`](../../front-end/public/licenses/chromium-bsd-license.txt)
- Checksums: [`front-end/src/vendor/chromium-t-rex/UPSTREAM_SHA256SUMS`](../../front-end/src/vendor/chromium-t-rex/UPSTREAM_SHA256SUMS)

## Vendored files

All 19 files from `components/neterror/resources/dino_game/`, the parent
`constants.ts`, `neterror.html`, and `neterror.css` are preserved byte for byte
under `upstream/`. Their local names end in `.txt` so the repository's normal
Vue type-check and lint passes do not reinterpret Chromium source that depends
on Chromium's own WebUI build system. Removing that final `.txt` restores each
upstream filename without changing its contents.

The two standard-resolution sprite sheets, two initial offline icons, and three
sound files are also exact upstream bytes. Chromium names the sound resources
with `.mp3` extensions even though the current files contain Ogg Vorbis audio;
the names and bytes are intentionally preserved.

Run this from the repository root to verify the upstream copies:

```sh
cd front-end/src/vendor/chromium-t-rex
shasum -a 256 -c UPSTREAM_SHA256SUMS
```

The complete Chromium BSD license is served from
`/licenses/chromium-bsd-license.txt`. Chromium and Google do not endorse or
sponsor this site.

## Standalone integration

Chromium normally bundles this game into its internal network-error page. The
following Avasan-owned compatibility layer makes that unchanged gameplay source
work as a regular site component:

- `compat/assert.ts` implements the assertion API used by Chromium modules.
- `compat/load-time-data.ts` supplies only the English accessibility strings
  normally generated by Chromium's WebUI localization pipeline.
- `compat/frame-entry.ts.txt` initializes `Runner` in the standalone frame.
- `frame.css` provides the game-only subset of the net-error page layout.
- `build-official-bundle.mjs` resolves the two `chrome://` imports and compiles
  the pristine TypeScript modules into `generated/chromium-t-rex-frame.js.txt`.
  During that derived build only, it removes Chromium's browser-controller
  telemetry and profile high-score hooks; the preserved upstream file stays
  byte exact.
- `index.ts` exports `mountChromiumTrex(host, options)`, embeds exact local
  sprites and sounds as data URLs, and returns an idempotent cleanup function.

Regenerate the derived browser bundle after an audited upstream update:

```sh
node front-end/src/vendor/chromium-t-rex/build-official-bundle.mjs
```

The production build independently regenerates that bundle in memory and
requires an exact byte match with the committed artifact. Stable virtual module
names keep the output identical across developer and server checkout paths; the
gate also rejects absolute filesystem paths in the shipped runtime.

The compatibility layer does not change obstacle generation, collision logic,
speed, in-session score calculation, controls, drawing, animation, or sound
behavior.

## Privacy and containment

The runner mounts in a `srcdoc` iframe sandboxed with `allow-scripts` and
without `allow-same-origin`. Chromium's document-wide keyboard, pointer,
visibility, resize, and animation handlers therefore remain inside the game
frame. Removing the iframe destroys that isolated browser realm and stops its
listeners and animation frames.

The frame adds a restrictive content-security policy: images and sounds must be
embedded data URLs, scripts and styles must be inline, and connections, frames,
workers, forms, fonts, and objects are blocked. The generated bundle is also
checked for fetch, XHR, WebSocket, beacon, cookie, and Web Storage APIs before
it is written.

Chromium's preserved source contains optional conditional calls to
`window.errorPageController` for Chrome profile statistics and high-score sync.
The local bundle builder removes those browser-only hooks and the associated
global high-score initializer from the derived runtime. Scores live only in the
isolated frame's memory for the current play session. There is no game
analytics, account association, cookie, local storage, session storage, or
third-party request.
